title: "Day 6. Cut-offs, two-cut-off designs and the intermediate zone"
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("../R/helpers.R")
suppressMessages({library(knitr); library(ggplot2); library(cutpointr); library(OptimalCutpoints); library(pROC)})
select <- dplyr::select
```

Tags: **[S]** primary public source, **[Y]** my synthesis, **[D]** derived by me by arithmetic from a cited count. The lab uses **simulated** data only.

## (a) Concept

| Idea | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Single cut-off | one threshold; Youden (max Se+Sp−1), a targeted Se or Sp, or cost-weighted |
| Two cut-offs | **rule-out** cut-off set for sensitivity/NPV; **rule-in** cut-off set for specificity/PPV |
| Intermediate ("grey") zone | results between the two; the price paid for high predictive values |
| Lock before validation | derive on one cohort, freeze, validate on another; never re-tune on validation data |
| Spectrum and prevalence | the same cut-offs give different zone fractions and PPV/NPV in primary vs specialty care |

Grey-zone approach: Coste & Pouchot, *Int J Epidemiol* 2003;32:304-313 [S: abstract]: a three-zone partition whose width depends on the separation of the group means, variability, and the accepted misclassification risks. TG-ROC plots sensitivity and specificity against the threshold so the zone limits can be read off.

## (b) Regulatory anchor and worked example: Elecsys Phospho-Tau (217P) Plasma

Facts below were read from the **FDA 510(k) Decision Summary K261686** (37 pp.) and re-checked by me against the PDF for the tables marked ✔. Everything else is from the research notes (`research/ptau217_notes.md`).

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 510(k) / decision | K261686, decision **2026-08-19**, SESE, Class II, 21 CFR 866.5840 "Alzheimer's Disease Pathology Assessment Test" | FDA-DS p.1, openFDA record |
| Predicate | Lumipulse G pTau 217/beta-Amyloid 1-42 Plasma Ratio, K242706 ✔ | FDA-DS p.4 |
| Indication | aid in identifying amyloid pathology in patients with cognitive decline, plasma of individuals ≥ 55 years, used with other clinical information ✔ | FDA-DS p.2 |
| Cut-offs (pg/mL) | **Negative ≤ 0.223; Intermediate > 0.223 to ≤ 0.378; Positive > 0.378** ✔ | FDA-DS p.3 |
| Cut-off derivation cohort | 687 banked samples; 286 PET+ (41.6%); the selection rule for 0.223/0.378 is **not stated** | FDA-DS p.20 |
| Pivotal cohort | N = 958; 378 PET+ (39.5%); reference = amyloid PET visual read by 6 blinded readers; CSF only as a tie-breaker | FDA-DS pp.22-26 |
| Monitoring / dementia prediction | **Not** in the decision summary; stated in the Roche 24 Aug 2026 release only | ROCHE-0824 |

**Pivotal 3×2 table** ✔ (FDA-DS p.26):

```{r fda-table}
fda <- matrix(c(285, 37, 72, 119, 21, 424), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE,
              dimnames = list(Assay = c("Positive (>0.378)", "Intermediate", "Negative (<=0.223)"),
                              `Amyloid PET` = c("PET+", "PET-")))
kable(addmargins(fda))
```

Reproduce what FDA reported, then compare **our** CI methods with theirs:

```{r fda-repro}
N <- sum(fda); pet_pos <- sum(fda[, 1]); pet_neg <- sum(fda[, 2])
rows <- list(
  c("PPA (positive among PET+)", 285, pet_pos, "75.4 (70.8-79.5)"),
  c("NPA (negative among PET-)", 424, pet_neg, "73.1 (69.4-76.6)"),
  c("PPV of positive", 285, 322, "88.5 (84.9-91.4)"),
  c("NPV of negative", 424, 445, "95.3 (93.1-96.8)"))
out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rows, function(r) {
  x <- as.numeric(r[2]); n <- as.numeric(r[3]); w <- ci_wilson(x, n); cp <- ci_clopper_pearson(x, n)
  data.frame(Measure = r[1], `FDA reported` = r[4],
             `Wilson` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", 100 * w[1], 100 * w[2], 100 * w[3]),
             `Clopper-Pearson` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", 100 * cp[1], 100 * cp[2], 100 * cp[3]),
             check.names = FALSE)}))
kable(out, caption = "FDA CIs vs ours. FDA states the PV CIs derive from likelihood-ratio CIs; the PPA/NPA CI method is not stated")
```

Our Wilson intervals reproduce FDA's PPA and NPA CIs to the printed digit (70.8-79.5, 69.4-76.6), so Wilson is the likely method [D: inference, not stated by FDA]. The PV CIs differ slightly because FDA derives them from likelihood-ratio CIs.

The **PPA/NPA are low (≈75%)** because intermediates count as misses (denominators include all PET+ and PET−). The headline strength is in the categories: **PV 88.5% for positive, 95.3% NPV for negative, 19.9% (191/958) intermediate** ✔. Derived by me [D] from the counts above (no CI in the FDA summary):

```{r derived}
d <- rbind(
  c("Rule-out step: not-negative among PET+ (357/378)", 357, 378),
  c("Rule-in step: not-positive among PET- (543/580)", 543, 580),
  c("Intermediate fraction (191/958)", 191, 958))
kable(data.frame(Quantity = d[, 1],
  `Estimate (Wilson 95% CI), %` = sapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i) {
    w <- ci_wilson(as.numeric(d[i, 2]), as.numeric(d[i, 3]))
    sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", 100 * w[1], 100 * w[2], 100 * w[3]) }), check.names = FALSE))
```

Also FDA's decision logic is worth noting: the **PV is judged "statistically higher than prevalence"** (lower CI bound 84.9% > prevalence 39.5%), a comparison with the prevalence rather than a pre-specified performance goal; none of a sample-size calculation or goal was found in the text read. ✔ (FDA-DS p.27)

**Known blemishes in the summary** (do not copy tables uncritically) ✔: p.26 says "pre-specified cut-offs of 0.225 pg/mL" while the table uses 0.223, and "prevalence 13.1%" in one sentence vs 39.5% elsewhere; others are listed in the notes.

**What the two papers do and do not give.** Both use the *prototype* assay, not the cleared one, and neither reports 0.223/0.378. *Hibar et al., Alzheimers Dement 2026;22(1):e71009*: five cohorts, N = 2,148, single rule-out cut-off 0.189 pg/mL, no intermediate zone; e.g. cognitively impaired (n = 538) sensitivity 98.98%, specificity 29.17%, NPV 92.51% [S]. *Hortsch et al., J Prev Alzheimers Dis 2026;13(5):100534*: APPROACH, N = 588, centiloid reference, exploratory double cut-off at 90% PPA / 90% NPA, **indeterminate 5.78% at centiloid 30**, Wilson CIs, eGFR distribution reported and "higher pTau217 with worse kidney function" [S]. Nothing here is the pivotal data behind the clearance.

## (c) R lab (simulated)

### Cohorts

pTau217-*like*: log10 concentration normal in both groups, higher in amyloid-positive.

```{r sim}
sim_cohort <- function(n, prev, seed, egfr_shift = FALSE) {
  set.seed(seed)
  y <- rbinom(n, 1, prev)
  lx <- ifelse(y == 1, rnorm(n, -0.20, 0.30), rnorm(n, -0.80, 0.25))
  egfr <- round(pmin(120, pmax(8, rnorm(n, 78, 22))))
  if (egfr_shift) lx <- lx + ifelse(egfr >= 60, 0, ifelse(egfr >= 30, 0.10, 0.30))  # assumed effect
  data.frame(y, x = 10^lx, egfr)
}
train <- sim_cohort(700, 0.40, 61)      # derivation cohort
valid <- sim_cohort(950, 0.40, 62)      # separate validation cohort
c(train_AUC = as.numeric(auc(roc(train$y, train$x, quiet = TRUE, direction = "<"))),
  valid_AUC = as.numeric(auc(roc(valid$y, valid$x, quiet = TRUE, direction = "<"))))
```

### Derive the two cut-offs on the derivation cohort

Targets (assumed): sensitivity ≥ 94% for the rule-out step, specificity ≥ 93% for the rule-in step, chosen to resemble the derived operating points of the public pivotal data. [Y]

```{r derive}
co <- derive_two_cutoffs(train$x, train$y, 0.94, 0.93)
# cross-check 1: cutpointr
a <- cutpointr(train, x, y, pos_class = 1, neg_class = 0, direction = ">=",
               method = maximize_metric, metric = spec_constrain, min_constrain = 0.94)
b <- cutpointr(train, x, y, pos_class = 1, neg_class = 0, direction = ">=",
               method = maximize_metric, metric = sens_constrain, min_constrain = 0.93)
# cross-check 2: OptimalCutpoints
oc_lo <- optimal.cutpoints(X = "x", status = "y", tag.healthy = 0, methods = "ValueSe",
                           control = control.cutpoints(valueSe = 0.94), data = train)
oc_hi <- optimal.cutpoints(X = "x", status = "y", tag.healthy = 0, methods = "ValueSp",
                           control = control.cutpoints(valueSp = 0.93), data = train)
pick <- function(o, nm) as.numeric(o$Global$optimal.cutoff[[nm]])[1]
oc_lo_c <- pick(oc_lo$ValueSe, "cutoff"); oc_lo_se <- pick(oc_lo$ValueSe, "Se")
oc_hi_c <- pick(oc_hi$ValueSp, "cutoff"); oc_hi_sp <- pick(oc_hi$ValueSp, "Sp")
se_at <- function(c) mean(train$x[train$y == 1] > c)
sp_at <- function(c) mean(train$x[train$y == 0] <= c)
kable(data.frame(
  Method = c("hand", "cutpointr", "OptimalCutpoints"),
  `Rule-out cut-off` = round(c(co[["lo"]], a$optimal_cutpoint, oc_lo_c), 4),
  `Sens at it` = round(c(se_at(co[["lo"]]), a$sensitivity, oc_lo_se), 4),
  `Rule-in cut-off` = round(c(co[["hi"]], b$optimal_cutpoint, oc_hi_c), 4),
  `Spec at it` = round(c(sp_at(co[["hi"]]), b$specificity, oc_hi_sp), 4),
  check.names = FALSE), caption = "Same targets, three tools")
```

Sensitivity is identical across the three at the rule-out step. The rule-in cut-offs can differ by one observation depending on each tool's tie and boundary convention (≥ versus >); the hand version fixes the FDA convention (positive if > cut-off). [Y]

```{r tgroc}
#| fig-height: 3.8
g <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(train$x)), function(t)
  data.frame(t = t, Sensitivity = mean(train$x[train$y == 1] > t), Specificity = mean(train$x[train$y == 0] <= t))))
gl <- rbind(data.frame(t = g$t, value = g$Sensitivity, Measure = "Sensitivity (x > t)"),
            data.frame(t = g$t, value = g$Specificity, Measure = "Specificity (x <= t)"))
ggplot(gl, aes(t, value, colour = Measure)) + geom_line() + scale_x_log10() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = unlist(co), linetype = 2) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = co[["lo"]], xmax = co[["hi"]], ymin = 0, ymax = 1, alpha = .08) +
  labs(x = "Threshold (pg/mL, log scale)", y = NULL, subtitle = "TG-ROC: shaded = intermediate zone") + theme_minimal()
```

For comparison, a single Youden cut-off on the same data:

```{r youden}
yc <- cutpointr(train, x, y, pos_class = 1, neg_class = 0, direction = ">=",
                method = maximize_metric, metric = youden)
data.frame(cutoff = yc$optimal_cutpoint, sens = yc$sensitivity, spec = yc$specificity)
```

### Lock, then validate

```{r validate}
p <- two_cut_performance(valid$x, valid$y, co[["lo"]], co[["hi"]])
fm <- function(v) sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", 100 * v[["est"]], 100 * v[["lower"]], 100 * v[["upper"]])
kable(addmargins(p$table), caption = "Validation cohort, cut-offs locked from the derivation cohort")
kable(data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Intermediate fraction", "Rule-out step sensitivity (not-negative among D+)", "Negative result NPV",
               "Rule-in step specificity", "Positive result PPV",
               "PPA incl. intermediates (FDA-summary style)", "NPA incl. intermediates"),
  `Estimate % (Wilson 95% CI)` = c(fm(p$intermediate), fm(p$ruleout_sens), fm(p$ruleout_npv),
                                    fm(p$rulein_spec), fm(p$rulein_ppv), fm(p$ppa_incl), fm(p$npa_incl)),
  check.names = FALSE))
```

How to state the claim when a result can be indeterminate (the FDA summary's practice [S]): report the **fraction** of intermediates, performance of each category, and PPA/NPA with intermediates counted as not-agreeing; the "excluding intermediates" figures alone flatter the test. [Y]

### Prevalence and spectrum change the zones

Same locked cut-offs, three populations: primary care (prev 20%), secondary (40%), memory clinic (60%).

```{r prev}
res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.20, 0.40, 0.60), function(pv) {
  v <- sim_cohort(20000, pv, 63)
  q <- two_cut_performance(v$x, v$y, co[["lo"]], co[["hi"]])
  data.frame(Prevalence = pv, `Intermediate %` = round(100 * q$intermediate[["est"]], 1),
             `PPV positive %` = round(100 * q$rulein_ppv[["est"]], 1),
             `NPV negative %` = round(100 * q$ruleout_npv[["est"]], 1), check.names = FALSE)}))
kable(res, caption = "Sens/spec per class unchanged; predictive values and zone fractions move")
```

The FDA summary itself reports lower PV of positive results in primary care (78.3%, 36/46) than secondary/tertiary (90.2%, 249/276) and a footnote about lower PPV in low-prevalence settings [S: FDA-DS pp.3, 32].

### Kidney function as a covariate (assumed effect)

The FDA summary has **no eGFR-stratified analysis** (only a kidney-disease comorbidity subgroup of N = 24) [S]. Hortsch et al. report higher pTau217 with worse kidney function in their prototype data [S]. Here: an *assumed* upward shift of the log marker in amyloid-negative *and* positive subjects with lower eGFR (+0.10 log10 for eGFR 30-59, +0.30 below 30); cut-offs stay locked.

```{r egfr}
kv <- sim_cohort(40000, 0.40, 64, egfr_shift = TRUE)
kv$stage <- cut(kv$egfr, c(0, 30, 60, Inf), right = FALSE, labels = c("<30", "30-59", ">=60"))
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(kv$stage), function(s) {
  v <- kv[kv$stage == s, ]
  q <- two_cut_performance(v$x, v$y, co[["lo"]], co[["hi"]])
  data.frame(eGFR = s, n = nrow(v), `Intermediate %` = round(100 * q$intermediate[["est"]], 1),
             `Rule-in specificity %` = round(100 * q$rulein_spec[["est"]], 1),
             `PPV positive %` = round(100 * q$rulein_ppv[["est"]], 1),
             `Rule-out sensitivity %` = round(100 * q$ruleout_sens[["est"]], 1), check.names = FALSE) }))
kable(tab, caption = "Effect of an assumed eGFR-dependent shift on locked cut-offs")
```

Reading: lower eGFR pushes controls into the intermediate and positive zones (specificity of the rule-in step and PPV fall) while sensitivity rises. Options to discuss: eGFR-stratified cut-offs, a flag on the report, or a pre-specified eGFR subgroup analysis in the SAP (Day 9). The size of the shift is my assumption. [Y]
